source_operations.before: 1.1 The matrix is nonnormal: $AA^{\mathsf T}=\begin{pmatrix}17&-4\\-4&1\end{pmatrix}$ while $A^{\mathsf T}A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-4\\-4&17\end{pmatrix}$. Its two eigenvalues are $-1$, so those of $hA$ are both $-1/2\in[-2,0]$ and the scalar stability factor is $1/2$. [F2, given, algebra]
source_operations.after: 1.1 The matrix is nonnormal: $AA^{\mathsf T}=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix}$ while $A^{\mathsf T}A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\-2&5\end{pmatrix}$. For every $u=(u_0,u_1)$, $\langle Au,u\rangle=-u_0^2+2u_0u_1-u_1^2=-(u_0-u_1)^2\le0$. Its two eigenvalues are $-1$, so $\rho=1$ and $h\rho=1/2\le2s^2$ for $s=1$. Both eigenvalues of $hA$ are $-1/2\in[-2,0]$ and the scalar stability factor is $1/2$. Thus the nonpositive quadratic-form and step-size premises of [F2] hold. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

source_operations.before: 2.1 The one-stage update is $I+hA=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&2\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.$ It sends $v=(0,1)$ to $(2,1/2)$, whose Euclidean norm is $\sqrt{17}/2>1=\|v\|_2$. Therefore eigenvalue-wise scalar stability does not imply a matrix norm bound here; the self-adjoint hypothesis in [F2] cannot be omitted. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
source_operations.after: 2.1 The one-stage update is $I+hA=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&1\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.$ It sends $v=(0,1)$ to $(1,1/2)$, whose Euclidean norm is $\sqrt5/2>1=\|v\|_2$. Therefore eigenvalue-wise scalar stability does not imply a matrix norm bound even with the nonpositive quadratic-form and step-size premises retained; the self-adjoint hypothesis in [F2] cannot be omitted. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
